newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway P.M. steps into European salmon dispute.
newsitem.headline: Norway P.M. steps into European salmon dispute.

text.p: Norway on Friday urged the European Commission not to impose anti-dumping duties on Norwegian salmon imports and called for renewed dialogue to solve the trade dispute.

Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland, in a letter to President of the European Commission Jacques Santer, said the matter may "lead to most unfortunate complications in the relations between the European Union and Norway".

"My main concern is of a political nature. I would find it extremely regrettable if the European Union decided to apply trade policy measures against a close political and economic partner such as Norway," Jagland wrote.
He reiterated that Norway saw no foundation to allegations that the country's salmon producers receive state subsidies and dump the fish on the EU market at less than the cost of production.

The EU executive is considering slapping an average duty of 13.7 percent on Norwegian salmon imports after the Commission launched an inquiry in September, looking into Scottish complaints that Norway was flooding the market and depressing prices.

The EU's anti-dumping committee -- which consists of officials from the 15 member states -- discussed the sensitive issue at a closed meeting in Brussels on Monday. A decision on is expected over the next few days.

Norway, whose voters rejected EU membership in 1994, is a member of the 18-nation European Economic Area agreement. The country's salmon exports to the European Union are worth some 5.5 billion crowns ($790 million) annually.

On Wednesday Norwegian Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal, in Brussels for talks with EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan, said Norway's salmon industry would suffer a major blow if punitive anti-dumping duties were imposed.
Jagland said the government wanted to contribute actively to find constructive solutions to improve the situation on the European salmon market.

"When this issue appears on the agenda of the Commission I urge you to contribute to a solution based on dialogue and cooperation rather than imposing trade policy measures. I pledge the readiness of my government to make the same contribution," the prime minister said.
